_note: Hand-verified corrections to extracted titles, applied by scripts/library-propose-references.py after all mechanical cleanup. Each entry records a title an agent read out of the document itself, or a demotion where the document does not contain its own title at all. This exists because the last few per cent of extraction defects are not worth another heuristic: a rule general enough to fix them starts eating real titles, which is how 'Modular curves, invariant theory and E8' briefly lost its E8.
_rules: A `title` override may only REMOVE text that is visibly not part of the title (a byline, a series banner) or repair spacing damage in text that is present. It may not supply a title the document does not contain.

When the document does not contain its own title — a journal offprint whose masthead replaced it — record `band: "low"` with a reason instead of guessing. arXiv, which would settle it, returns 403 from this environment.
Say what was removed in `why`, so a reviewer can check the call without opening the PDF.

An `authors` override replaces a parsed author list. Same rule as titles: it may only repair names visible in the document (a kerning split, an affiliation letter welded to a surname), never supply names the document does not show.

A `title` accompanied by `title_source` came from OUTSIDE the document text — normally the filename an uploader assigned — and is only permitted when the document's own content corroborates it (author, journal, volume, year all agreeing). Say so in `title_source`. Without corroboration, demote instead.
`drop_authors: true` discards a parsed author list outright, for documents where the author field held something else — the title, or a masthead — so the parse is meaningless rather than imprecise.
